name: Christian corporatism
summary: Christian corporatism holds that society is an organic body in which employers and workers of each industry or profession should be joined in cooperating vocational groups under a neutral, subsidiary state, in place of class struggle. It defends private property with a social duty, a family wage and wide ownership, and rejects both liberal individualism and socialism as a third course grounded in Christian morality and the Church.
scope: The Catholic corporatism of Rerum novarum (1891) and Quadragesimo anno (1931), with Heinrich Pesch's solidarism and Oswald von Nell-Breuning behind it, and the Austrian Standestaat of Dollfuss and Schuschnigg as its main applied case. It excludes Protestant corporatism such as Kuyper's, Mussolini's totalitarian corporate state, and postwar democratic neo-corporatism. Where Catholic doctrine and the Austrian regime diverge, such as on party monopoly and parliament, answers are neutral or low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Pope Leo XIII
keyFigures.role: Author of Rerum novarum, which founded modern Catholic social teaching on class cooperation and workers' associations.

keyFigures.name: Pope Pius XI
keyFigures.role: Author of Quadragesimo anno, which promoted vocational-group corporatism as an alternative to capitalism and socialism.

keyFigures.name: Heinrich Pesch
keyFigures.role: Jesuit economist whose solidarism was the most influential Catholic version of corporatism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pius XI says free competition has destroyed itself and that economic life must be ruled by social justice and charity, though private enterprise stays.

public-ownership.rationale: The state is to direct, watch and restrain rather than own; private property is defended against collectivism, so nationalisation is not a doctrinal aim.

unions-good.rationale: Rerum novarum calls workers' associations the most important of all associations, though the corporatist ideal replaces class-only unions with mixed vocational bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rerum novarum 6 holds that every man has by nature a right to own property, and Quadragesimo anno 49 says the state may regulate its use but not abolish it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Leo XIII says the poor deserve the state's special protection, so cutting welfare contradicts the doctrine, though charity and subsidiarity are preferred to state dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Pius XI prefers partnership contracts that share ownership or profit with workers, but Leo XIII rejects community of goods, so collective worker ownership of firms is not the model.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents split: the Austrian regime restricted opponents' speech, but Catholic doctrine does not address hate-speech law as such.

strong-leader.rationale: Dollfuss suspended parliament and ruled by decree, yet Catholic theory stresses subsidiarity and neutral state authority rather than a leader, so this is a regime-based inference.

state-harmful.rationale: Rerum novarum 32 makes it the state's main duty to frame laws and institutions that promote public well-being, so a corporatist treats the state as necessary and good.

limit-guns.rationale: Neither encyclical addresses firearms; adherents have no settled position.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Austrian corporate state relied on the army, police and Heimwehr, but funding of the forces is not doctrinally discussed.

rehabilitation.rationale: Catholic thought values both reform and just punishment, and the sources do not choose between them.

traditional-family.rationale: Rerum novarum 13-14 calls the family a true society prior to the state with its own rights and paternal authority, and Quadragesimo anno 71 ties the wage to family needs.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Christian corporatism rests on the family as the social cell as Rerum novarum describes it; the question is modern but the Catholic answer follows directly.

more-religion-public.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 129 says only a return to Christian life and institutions will heal society, so religion must shape public life.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Rerum novarum 42 treats a woman's fitness for home work as natural, so adherents see sex roles as grounded in nature.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pesch's solidarism treats patriotism as one of the organic solidarities of society, and the Austrian regime was built on a patriotic Fatherland Front.

gradual-change.rationale: Christian corporatism arose in counter-revolutionary Catholic circles that wanted guild-like institutions grown from the old order, not rupture.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Pesch's solidarism includes internationalism, but corporatism centres on national vocational bodies; adherents are split.

nation-first.rationale: Solidarism pairs patriotism with international solidarity, so adherents do not clearly side either way.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Pius XI says moral and spiritual renewal, not technical means, is the first remedy for social disorder.

revolution-justified.rationale: Leo XIII tells workers to avoid violence and agitators, and corporatism was counter-revolutionary in origin.

experts-over-public.rationale: Vocational groups are organised by social function and Pesch's national economic council was meant to advise parliament, giving weight to those with functional expertise.

central-planning.rationale: Pius XI judges socialism a remedy worse than the evil and defends private ownership; a centrally planned economy is the socialist form of this.

socialized-markets.rationale: Leo XIII rejects community of goods and defends private ownership, so ownership by the public is not a doctrinal route.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Rerum novarum 13 defends inheritance as the father's means of providing for his children, so heavy inheritance tax cuts against it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 58-61 condemns the gulf between a few rich and the propertyless and wants workers able to acquire property through thrift.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rerum novarum 44-45 treats the wage as the due of labour and says it must support the worker, so wage labour is accepted, not abolished.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 83-87 proposes vocational groups of employers and workers with legal standing; the state-recognised form is the core institution, though Pius XI voices reservations about Italy's version.

one-party-rule.rationale: Dollfuss made the Fatherland Front the only legal party, but Catholic doctrine itself prescribes no single party, so adherents are split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a monarch who rules, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state, on which the sources cited here are silent.

reviewHistory.rationale: Counter-revolutionary Catholics accepted monarchy, and doctrine is neutral on regime form; not directly stated.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a monarch who rules, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state, on which the sources cited here are silent.

democracy-best.rationale: Early Christian corporatists opposed liberal democracy and the Austrian corporate state ended parliamentary democracy, though some strands accept it.

direct-votes.rationale: Representation through organic bodies rather than mass plebiscite follows from the counter-revolutionary roots of the doctrine.

workers-councils.rationale: Corporatist bodies join employers and workers by function; councils of workers alone as the basis of power contradict that.

political-violence-never.rationale: Leo XIII urges workers to avoid violence, yet the Austrian regime used force in February 1934 and Catholic just-war thinking allows it.

separate-church-state.rationale: The article says Christian corporatism arose in opposition to secularism and anticlericalism, and Leo XIII says no solution succeeds without the Church.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholic doctrine draws law from natural law and the Church, not scripture alone, but the Austrian order claimed a religious basis.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Leo XIII makes justice and public order the state's first duties, so privatising them contradicts the doctrine.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Fatherland Front advocated no racial ideology and included Jewish veterans, and Leo XIII affirms equal dignity before God.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rerum novarum 19 calls class conflict unnatural and Quadragesimo anno 112 condemns unrelenting class warfare.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rerum novarum 17 says unequal fortune follows necessarily from natural unequal condition, rejecting levelling.

civilizational-union.rationale: Christian solidarity could favour unity, but nothing is stated; adherents split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Pius XI warns against individualism and makes social charity the soul of economic order.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Pesch's solidarism puts community and mutual obligation first, but the encyclicals also affirm natural personal rights.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Pius XI criticises the effects of liberal industrialism but not industry as such.

restore-past-order.rationale: Pius XI calls for a return to Christian institutions and a revival of vocational groups modelled on the medieval guilds.

direct-action.rationale: Pius XI says strikes and lockouts are forbidden in the corporative order, with disputes settled through the vocational bodies.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Never discussed, but wholly at odds with the doctrine's defence of property, labour and family.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The organic body model of 1 Corinthians 12 depends on distinct social functions working together.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Leo XIII ties income to wages for work and sets relief of need under charity, not strict justice.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Leo XIII says capital needs labour and labour capital and rejects the Marxist reading, though he condemns defrauding workers of wages.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 112 condemns communism as impious and iniquitous.

collective-farming.rationale: Rerum novarum 9 and 15 say land worked by a person's labour becomes his own and reject common ownership.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Pius XI links concentrated economic power to conflict between states, yet rejects the Marxist inevitability claim; adherents split.

taxation-theft.rationale: Leo XIII gives the state a duty to promote public well-being, which taxation funds.

harm-principle.rationale: Pius XI makes moral reform the first remedy, so the state may act for the common good beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rerum novarum 13-14 and 50 give families and associations rights of their own, and Quadragesimo anno 45 stresses the social character of property.

state-as-business.rationale: Leo XIII defines the state's role as promoting public well-being, not serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Leo XIII insists wages be enough to live and save, implying material means matter, though liberty language is not used.

organic-representation.rationale: Quadragesimo anno and Pesch propose vocational groups and layered economic bodies up to a national council; these are economic bodies, and political representation through them appears mainly in the Austrian 1934 constitution.

total-state.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 79-80 sets subsidiarity, with the state leaving matters to lesser groups, and Rerum novarum 35 forbids the state absorbing individuals or families.

national-rebirth.rationale: Pius XI calls for a renewal of the Christian spirit and a return to Christian institutions to cure social decline.

bound-labor.rationale: Leo XIII treats labour as personal and the worker as owed a living wage and dignity, which excludes bondage.

universal-morality.rationale: Leo XIII appeals to natural right and the common order given by nature and God, which is universal.

single-common-good.rationale: Pius XI calls for harmonious cooperation under the common good, but accepts distinct group interests in vocational bodies.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Neither the encyclicals nor the Austrian regime's record touch a diaspora's right of return.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Pesch backed codetermination, but a democratic public vote on company management is not part of the doctrine; adherents split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Pius XI's economics concern the order of industry, not fiscal policy, so adherents have no settled view.

rule-by-example.rationale: Leo XIII stresses moral formation but also the state's law-making duty; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 127 and 129 say social reform requires renewal of the Christian spirit and return to Christian life, rejecting reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Leo XIII urges care for the poor of the community but never says whether non-citizens share it.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Leo XIII values work and the duty to labour yet protects the poor; no settled position.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rerum novarum 19 says capital cannot do without labour nor labour without capital, and Quadragesimo anno 81 asks the state to promote harmony between industries and professions.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Christian corporatism looks to medieval and Church institutions as its source, so sacrificing inherited institutions is rejected.

workers-nation.rationale: Quadragesimo anno groups workers by industry within the nation, not as an international class, and Pesch affirms patriotism.

ban-interest.rationale: Leo XIII condemns rapacious usury but does not call for banning moderate interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Rerum novarum 40 affirms equal dignity of all before God, and the Fatherland Front had no racial ideology.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 80 casts the state as a neutral directing and restraining authority above classes.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Rerum novarum 13 and 42 present paternal authority and women's domestic role as natural, not as systematic disadvantage.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Never addressed in the sources, but Rerum novarum 14 shields family rights from state absorption and Catholic doctrine upholds dignity.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rerum novarum 33 and 37 require the state to actively look after workers and shield the poor, far beyond defence and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Rerum novarum 40 affirms equal dignity before God, and the Austrian regime had no racial ideology.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rerum novarum 40 says rich and poor, master and servant are equal in soul and in right before God, though corporatist order is hierarchical.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no bearing on corporatism.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Irrelevant to the doctrine; adherents would not support it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Rerum novarum 14 protects the family's authority over upbringing and the Church's role, so religion belongs in schools.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority is traced to God, as in the Austrian order founded in God's name, rather than to consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Rerum novarum 40 affirms equal dignity for all, which forbids forced removals.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Leo XIII gives the state a rightful role in law and order, so a blanket ban on initiating force is not accepted.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Pius XI says free competition has destroyed itself and seeks harmony between classes, not struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Dollfuss banned the Communist, Nazi and Social Democratic parties, and Quadragesimo anno 112 condemns communism.

separated-powers.rationale: Subsidiarity pluralises authority, yet the Austrian regime concentrated power; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leo XIII warns workers against agitators and holds class harmony to be natural.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rerum novarum 37 says the poor, lacking resources, deserve the special protection of the state.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 94 describes the Italian corporative system, in which strikes and lockouts are forbidden, and notes it with some reservations rather than endorsing it; the tradition leans toward settling disputes through vocational bodies instead of strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Pius XI blames unjust distribution and concentrated economic power, not numbers.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Dollfuss suspended parliament in 1933 and banned parties, so the regime used emergency measures against internal enemies.

party-controls-media.rationale: The sources do not document media control; adherents split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Pesch's internationalism and later Catholic support for European union conflict with national corporatist regimes.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic doctrine on Church government is episcopal and hierarchical.

clerical-rule.rationale: Pius XI assigns the Church the moral guidance of society and the state its own neutral role, rather than rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Leo XIII calls for order, loyalty and harmony and counters revolutionaries, ruling out defeatism.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Pius XI wants wide ownership but never proposes banning rent; the claim is too radical for the doctrine.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources make no claim about the educated; adherents have no settled view.

death-penalty.rationale: Catholic thought has historically allowed it for grave crimes but with growing reservations; no settled position.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Parental authority over upbringing (Rerum novarum 14) makes state-mandated curricula suspect.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Austrian regime rewrote the constitution by a rump session without a new election.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Pius XI binds the wealthy to almsgiving and charity, though he addresses classes within nations, not states.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 45-49 says ownership has an individual and social character and the state may regulate its use for the common good but not abolish the right.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is not treated in the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Authority comes from God but Leo XIII affirms all are equal before God; no ruler is divine.

character-from-environment.rationale: Rerum novarum 17 stresses natural differences in ability and strength.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rerum novarum 32 makes laws and institutions serve public well-being, binding rulers to a moral order.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rerum novarum 9 and 13 defend land and inheritance as private property earned by labour.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Historical confessional views and later Catholic liberty teaching split adherents.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 98 and 127 call moral and spiritual renewal the first remedy, rejecting the claim that economics alone drives social change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Pius XI condemns concentrated economic power but wants guild-like industry bodies, not free competition, so adherents are split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Rerum novarum 42 sees distinct roles, which undercuts parity quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Fascist Italy pursued autarky, but Catholic sources do not endorse it.

moral-incentives.rationale: Social charity is the soul of the order but wages remain the reward of work.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Leo XIII condemns violence and agitators; the doctrine is counter-revolutionary.

public-money-creation.rationale: Pius XI attacks private control of credit but offers no remedy on money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Pius XI proposes reforming economic life through vocational groups, not awaiting collapse, and rejects Marxist inevitability.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist claim; corporatism holds that workers and employers share common interest.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Catholic tradition allows resistance to tyranny, yet the regime enforced obedience; split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Austrian corporate state suspended and curtailed parliament, and corporatists prefer functional bodies.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 50 says those with superfluous income are bound by a very grave precept to give alms.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Pius XI calls Christians to take part in social reconstruction.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Austrian regime banned both Communists and Nazis, and Quadragesimo anno condemns communism and criticises state over-reach.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical dispute with no bearing on the sources.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Austrian regime rested on the army, but the doctrine does not assign it a political role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Pius XI sets a family wage so mothers need not work outside the home, valuing domestic labour, but he does not propose paying it.

filial-duty.rationale: Rerum novarum 13-14 treats the family as a society with authority and obligations between generations.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The family as a lasting society (Rerum novarum 13) and Catholic teaching on marriage's indissolubility oppose it.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Rerum novarum 6 and 9 defend individual ownership of land one has worked.

corporate-influence.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 105-108 says concentrated economic power struggles to control the state, which matches complaints of corporate influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Pius XI's family wage is meant to let workers raise families with ease, supporting family incentives.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Authority comes from God and laws promote the common good, so a general duty to obey is the default.

industrial-unions.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 83-85 organises vocational groups by industry and profession rather than craft alone.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Fatherland Front advocated no racial ideology and welcomed Jewish veterans.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Rerum novarum 13 treats the family and its property as foundational and protected.

informal-organisation.rationale: Corporatism favours structured vocational bodies with legal standing, not informal groups.

religious-nation.rationale: The Austrian order was Catholic by design, though doctrine does not define the nation by religion.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The statement endorses common ownership of production, which Rerum novarum 15 rejects.

defeat-communism.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 112-120 treats communism as impious and irreconcilable with Catholic teaching, and Austria's regime banned it.

religion-illusion.rationale: Rerum novarum 16 says all striving is vain without the Church and that religion shapes conduct laws cannot reach.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Pius XI accepts private enterprise but says liberal competition destroyed itself; adherents split on its progressive role.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rerum novarum 42 gives women a distinct domestic role; the statement's premise is not shared.

socialized-care.rationale: Rerum novarum 14 says paternal authority can be neither abolished nor absorbed by the state and the family precedes it.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Rerum novarum 15 rejects community of goods, which the proposed communities would practise.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The article says Quadragesimo anno promoted corporatism as an alternative to both capitalist individualism and socialist totalitarianism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Fatherland Front opposed Nazism and included Jewish veterans; denial has no place in the doctrine.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Dollfuss banned rival parties, yet Rerum novarum 50 holds that private associations have a right to exist; adherents split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Austrian order was founded on Catholic principles, and older confessional doctrine allowed such laws.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Leo XIII counsels order and obedience to authority and rejects violence.

alienated-labor.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 83 says labour is not a mere commodity and objects to the labour market dividing men into camps.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Austrian corporate state claimed a religious foundation and Catholic doctrine derives authority from God.

social-market-economy.rationale: Catholic solidarism influenced German social-market thinking, combining markets with social protection and rules.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Austrian regime relied on its army; Catholic teaching allows just defence.

reification.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 83 says labour is not a commodity, but this Marxist theory is not adopted.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Fatherland Front advocated no racial ideology, and Rerum novarum 40 affirms equal dignity.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Fatherland Front included Jewish groups and had no racial ideology.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Functional bodies, not random assemblies, are the corporatist vehicle.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Pius XI calls for a return to Christian institutions, not for adapting doctrine to modern conditions.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 105-109 describes an immense power and despotic economic dictatorship in few hands and says free competition destroyed itself.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Rerum novarum 16 holds that society cannot do without the Church and religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Leo XIII makes public order a state duty.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Rerum novarum 22 and 29 value charity, but 33 and 37 also require the state to protect the poor; adherents are split.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Catholic doctrine reserves the priesthood to men and the hierarchy is episcopal.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Rerum novarum 13 gives the father paternal authority within the family.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Rerum novarum 9 grounds property in labour, but returns on property are accepted; adherents split.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Rerum novarum 42 treats sex differences as natural.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Rerum novarum 42 treats womanhood as a natural category with a home role.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Pius XI treats social recovery as a matter of Christian renewal against moral decline.

culture-before-state.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 98 and 127 put moral and spiritual renewal first, before institutional reform.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Fatherland Front welcomed Jewish members and had no ethnic programme.

decide-locally.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 79-80 sets subsidiarity, leaving to smaller bodies what they can do, though corporatism organises by vocation and nation rather than by locality alone.

family-wage.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 71 requires a wage sufficient to support the worker and his family, and Rerum novarum 45 says it must keep a frugal worker.

independent-unions.rationale: Rerum novarum 48-49 defends workers' freedom to form associations and says the state must not suppress them, though the Austrian regime merged unions into a state-run body.

municipal-property.rationale: Rerum novarum defends private property as natural; the Church favours wide ownership by individuals and families, not ownership by the town.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Subsidiarity favours local decision, but corporatism organises by vocation and gives binding powers to national bodies; adherents are split.

person-over-state.rationale: Rerum novarum 6-7 says man is older than the state, which exists to protect the person and the family, and Quadragesimo anno 79 limits the state by subsidiarity.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 129 says social renewal needs a return to Christian life, so politics must serve spiritual needs as well as material ones.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Subsidiarity protects lower bodies, but the Austrian Standestaat centralised power; adherents are split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Catholic corporatism is organised around vocational groups and the Church, not language; the Austrian Standestaat called Austria German but the sources do not make language the test of nationhood.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Austrian regime faced real Nazi pressure on its independence, but Catholic doctrine itself does not frame foreign partition plots; split between the case and the doctrine.

capital-controls.rationale: Quadragesimo anno condemns the international imperialism of money and the dominance of finance, so state limits on capital movement fit; it proposes no explicit controls.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Pius XI wants employers and workers in each trade bound by common rules through joint vocational bodies, which is collective regulation of pay, though under corporative rather than union-versus-employer bargaining.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Quadragesimo anno condemns the international imperialism of money and calls for just economic relations among nations; the inference to favouring developing countries is weak.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The corporatist order works through the existing neutral state and vocational bodies; revolutionary destruction of the state is rejected as socialist.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Quadragesimo anno proposes a definite corporative order as the third course between individualism and socialism, not open experimentation.

sacred-nation.rationale: Catholic corporatists valued patriotism but placed God and the Church above the nation; the Austrian regime stressed a Christian German state, so views on a sacred nation are mixed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rerum novarum grounds worker dignity and natural rights in a common human nature created by God, which is not to be altered.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The movement is grounded in Catholic doctrine and the Church's claim to truth; Pius XI treats the Church as the guide of social morality, which does not fit all religions expressing one truth.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Catholic doctrine on nuclear arms postdates its key texts and the Austrian regime predates them; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

workers-own-party.rationale: The doctrine seeks class cooperation in mixed vocational groups of employers and workers, and Quadragesimo anno rejects class struggle; the Austrian regime banned party rivals and the workers' party.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Quadragesimo anno builds mixed vocational groups of employers and workers, and the Austrian Standestaat used a single compulsory union front, so mandatory membership is not rejected as strongly as a free-choice view would require.

voter-id.rationale: Neither the encyclicals nor the Austrian regime address voter ID, so the answer is neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Quadragesimo anno ties social order to the Catholic Church's teaching and the Austrian Standestaat gave the Catholic Church a privileged role, so equal recognition is rejected.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Christian corporatism sets representation through vocational groups and Austria ruled by decree after banning parties, so a purely electoral definition is rejected.

premarital-sex.rationale: Catholic teaching in Rerum novarum and Quadragesimo anno defends the family and marriage as the basis of order, so sex outside marriage is not acceptable.

women-suffrage.rationale: Quadragesimo anno is largely silent on women's vote and Austria's regime removed party politics, while Catholic doctrine later accepted it; adherents are split.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The corporatist outlook holds religion to be a support of order and the family, and rejects the claim that it oppresses anyone.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Catholic doctrine affirms scripture's inspiration but reads it within Church tradition, not as a literalist standard; the movement does not take a position on this.

defend-planned-state.rationale: It rejects socialism and state economic control as a third course, so it would not defend a nationalised planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: Its model of vocational groups and corporative chambers sends representatives chosen by occupational bodies, and the Austrian Standestaat replaced direct parliamentary elections with such bodies.

national-church-status.rationale: The Austrian Standestaat under Dollfuss and Schuschnigg privileged the Catholic Church, and the doctrine holds that society should rest on the Church's moral teaching.

simple-living.rationale: Rerum novarum praises frugality in workers but also defends property and a family wage, so no firm position is stated.

self-ownership.rationale: Quadragesimo anno treats the person as part of an organic social body with duties to the common good, rejecting liberal individualism.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Rerum novarum says the state should give special care to the poor, who depend on it more than the wealthy do.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Corporatism builds on vocational groups as intermediate bodies under subsidiarity, so it does not bypass groups.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Quadragesimo anno holds that distribution must serve justice and the common good, not whatever free competition produces.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Catholic natural-law tradition holds that human law cannot override the moral law, and Rerum novarum places the person above the state.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Quadragesimo anno rejects the view that labour alone, or capital alone, produces wealth and says the two need each other.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Quadragesimo anno rejects socialism outright, and the Austrian regime banned the left.

police-more-powers.rationale: The Austrian corporate state relied on the army, police and Heimwehr, but funding of the forces is not doctrinally discussed. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Leo XIII says the poor deserve the state's special protection, so cutting welfare contradicts the doctrine, though charity and subsidiarity are preferred to state dependency. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A worker's wage should be enough to support the worker and his family.
missingStatements.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 71 requires a wage sufficient to support the worker and his family, and Rerum novarum 45 says it must keep a frugal worker.

missingStatements.text: The state should leave to smaller communities and associations whatever they can do themselves, and step in only to direct and support.
missingStatements.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 79-80 sets out the subsidiary function: larger bodies must not take over what smaller ones can do, and the state directs, watches, urges and restrains.

missingStatements.text: Strikes and lockouts should be forbidden and disputes settled through joint bodies of employers and workers.
missingStatements.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 94 describes the corporative order as one in which strikes and lockouts are not allowed, with disputes handled inside the vocational groups.

notes: Statements on modern issues are mostly inferred from Catholic social teaching, so many answers are low confidence. The Austrian regime (single party, rule by decree) and Quadragesimo anno's neutral subsidiary state diverge on democracy and party monopoly. Protestant corporatism (Kuyper) would answer some religion and democracy items differently.
